title: Charging a Ridgecrest Advantage Coverage Month to a Member Who Holds a Low Income Premium Subsidy
content:
Where a closing settlement on a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan still charges for a coverage month, the share of the monthly plan premium charged to the member for that coverage month follows the low income premium subsidy recorded for the member on their Stand-Alone Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Plans record.

1. Where that record shows a full subsidy, none of the monthly plan premium is charged, that is 0 per cent of it.
2. Where that record shows a seventy-five per cent subsidy, a quarter of it is charged, that is 25 per cent of it.
3. Where that record shows a fifty per cent subsidy, half of it is charged, that is 50 per cent of it.
4. Where that record shows a twenty-five per cent subsidy, three quarters of it are charged, that is 75 per cent of it.
5. Where that record shows no subsidy at all, the whole of it is charged, that is 100 per cent of it.

The five entries above are the whole of the ladder, and the drug plan record is what settles which of them governs.

*Hypothetical case.* On a monthly plan premium of 100.00 USD for the plan held, a full subsidy on the drug plan record leaves 0.00 USD charged for the coverage month; a seventy-five per cent subsidy leaves 25.00 USD charged; a fifty per cent subsidy leaves 50.00 USD; a twenty-five per cent subsidy leaves 75.00 USD; and a record showing no subsidy at all leaves the full 100.00 USD charged.
